title: Minimum Wage in Aus: Hourly to Annual Pay for a 38-Hour Week
description: Convert the minimum wage in aus to annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. See how $26.44/hr becomes $52,254/year for a 38-hour week, plus super and tax estimates.
salarySummary: Based on the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, a 38-hour week yields $1,004.90 per week, $2,009.80 per fortnight, and $52,254.40 per year before tax and super.

faqs.q: How is annual pay calculated from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is hourly × 38 × 52. For example, the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour gives $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,254.40 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime or penalty rates.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect the minimum wage in aus?
faqs.a: Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for lack of paid leave. For the National Minimum Wage, the casual rate is $26.44 × 1.25 = $33.05 per hour. A casual working 38 hours per week would earn $33.05 × 38 × 52 = $65,317.60 per year before tax. The loading is paid on top of the base rate, so you should enter the base rate in a calculator and tick the casual loading box rather than entering a rate that already includes it.

faqs.q: How does superannuation work with the minimum wage?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid by your employer on top of your ordinary earnings at a rate of 12% (from 1 July 2026). It is not deducted from your gross pay. For a minimum-wage employee earning $52,254.40 per year, the employer would contribute an additional $6,270.53 into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. Super is calculated on ordinary time earnings, so casual loading is included if applicable.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage or have a salary offer, the simplest way to compare them is to convert your hourly rate to an annual figure. The standard formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This article assumes a 38-hour week, which is the full-time benchmark used by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the Australian Bureau of Statistics. If you work a different number of hours, adjust the formula accordingly. For a quick estimate, you can use [the timesheet](/), where you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading.

### The National Minimum Wage in Aus

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage set by the Fair Work Commission is **$26.44 per hour**. For a 38-hour week, that equates to:

- **Weekly:** $1,004.90
- **Fortnightly:** $2,009.80 (weekly × 2)
- **Annual:** $52,254.40

This is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or registered agreement. Many workers are covered by award rates, which can be higher. Always check your specific award or agreement. For more details, see our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page.

### Fortnightly Pay and Budgeting

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. Knowing your fortnightly amount helps with budgeting and comparing job offers. For the minimum wage, the fortnightly gross is $2,009.80. After tax and Medicare, the take-home amount will be lower. Use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide for estimates.

### Tax and Superannuation

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax rates:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15¢ for each $1 over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: 30¢ for each $1 over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: 37¢ for each $1 over $135,000
- $190,001+: 45¢ for each $1 over $190,000

A Medicare levy of 2% applies (using the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds as the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed). For a minimum-wage earner on $52,254.40, the estimated tax is $6,196.32 plus Medicare of $1,045.09, leaving a net annual pay of approximately $45,013. This is an estimate only; it does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

**Superannuation** is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. From 1 July 2026, the super guarantee rate is 12%, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For the minimum wage, the employer contributes an extra $6,270.53 per year into your super fund. Super is not deducted from your gross pay; it is an additional cost to your employer. Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Award Rates and Average Earnings

The National Minimum Wage is the floor, but many employees earn more under award rates or enterprise agreements. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports Average Weekly Earnings for full-time adult ordinary time as **$2,083.70 per week** (May 2026). This is an average across all industries and occupations, not a median for a specific job. All employees total earnings (including part-time) average $1,579.20 per week. For industry or state averages, refer to our [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page.

### Casual Loading

Casual employees receive a 25% loading on the base hourly rate to compensate for not receiving paid leave. The casual minimum wage is **$33.05 per hour** ($26.44 × 1.25). For a 38-hour week, a casual earns:

- **Weekly:** $1,256.10
- **Fortnightly:** $2,512.20
- **Annual:** $65,317.60

When using a calculator, enter the base rate (e.g., $26.44) and tick the casual loading box. Do not enter a rate that already includes loading. See our [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) guide for more.

### Important Assumptions

The annual pay shown here is an estimate based on the formula hourly × hours per week × 52. It assumes:

- The same hourly rate every week
- No unpaid overtime
- No penalty rates or allowances
- No salary sacrifice

Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted.

This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax. For personalised advice, consult a qualified professional or use official tools from the Fair Work Ombudsman, Australian Taxation Office, or your super fund.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

To convert your own hourly rate, visit [the timesheet](/). Enter your base hourly rate. If you are a casual employee, check the box to add 25% casual loading. The calculator will show your weekly, fortnightly, and annual figures before tax and super. You can then estimate your take-home pay using our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page.

Remember that award rates may be higher than the minimum. Always check your pay guide or agreement. For more resources, see our [pay guides](/blog) and [reference tables](/data).
